items.title: CVE-2026-109618 Impact of Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) on Palo Alto Networks Products  (Severity: CRITICAL)
items.one_liner: Critical PHP remote code execution vulnerabilities actively target internet-exposed Palo Alto Networks management interfaces.
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks has evaluated its product portfolio regarding two critical PHP remote code execution vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. CVE-2026-109618 stems from uninitialized request memory during longjmp() OOM handling, while CVE-2026-109619 leaves global memory pointing to freed regions during fatal error handling. PAN-OS software on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls, along with Panorama, are affected when management interfaces are exposed to the internet, and active exploitation has been observed. Palo Alto assigned the issue a critical CVSS score of 9.2, deployed patches for SaaS services like Cortex XCORE and WildFire Cloud, and released Threat ID 543004 for virtual patching and Threat Prevention users.
items.bottom_line: Active exploitation of critical PHP RCE vulnerabilities targets Palo Alto firewall management interfaces, requiring immediate threat signatures or access restrictions.

items.title: CVE-2026-46300: Linux Linux Kernel Missing Initialization of a Variable Vulnerability
items.one_liner: A Linux kernel variable initialization flaw (CVE-2026-46300) allowing remote code execution and root compromise via socket buffer chaining enters CISA's KEV.
items.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-46300, a missing variable initialization vulnerability in the Linux Kernel, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The flaw stems from a failure to preserve the shared-fragment marker during socket buffer coalescing, permitting unintended modifications to page-cache-backed data and causing ESP input processing to decrypt shared fragments in place. When chained with CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, attackers can implant PHP webshells and execute commands as root. Federal agencies are mandated to apply vendor mitigations or discontinue use by October 31, 2026.
key_facts: CVE-2026-46300: Linux Kernel missing variable initialization vulnerability
items.bottom_line: Linux kernel socket buffer vulnerabilities are actively tracked and require immediate patching to prevent root-level command execution chains.

items.title: Cisco Secure Firewall Adaptive Security Appliance and Secure Firewall Threat Defense Software Remote Access SSL VPN Tunnel Denial of Service Vulnerability

items.summary: A vulnerability in the Remote Access SSL VPN service of Cisco Secure Firewall Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) Software and Cisco Secure Firewall Threat Defense (FTD) Software could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause the device to reload unexpectedly, resulting in a denial of service condition. items.title: Volt Typhoon Used Silent Train to Hide Zero-Day Attacks
items.one_liner: Volt Typhoon's Silent Train covert network uses disposable multi-hop proxy chains and undisclosed zero-days to conceal critical attacks.
items.summary: Lumen's Black Lotus Labs revealed that the China-linked APT group Volt Typhoon utilized a covert relay network called Silent Train to hide attacks exploiting at least four zero-day vulnerabilities. Active since November 2023, the network abandoned persistent infrastructure in favor of disposable chains of compromised small-office routers, IoT devices, and enterprise appliances. Each session routed traffic through an average of four to six devices—originating outside the U.S. and passing through a final U.S. node to spoof local traffic and bypass reputation filters. The attackers installed temporary SSH access and completely dismantled traces within hours of session completion.
items.bottom_line: Volt Typhoon concealed zero-day attacks on critical infrastructure using disposable multi-hop relay chains of compromised SOHO and IoT devices.

The malware employs DLL sideloading to execute payloads while avoiding traditional C2 infrastructure by leveraging services like Telegram and Tor.

items.title: PHP2Shell: No login, no app code, no warning. What next?
items.one_liner: Critical PHP2Shell remote code execution flaws demand urgent enterprise-wide asset discovery and patching.
items.summary: Two critical PHP core vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, dubbed "PHP2Shell," allow unauthenticated remote attackers to execute code via crafted web requests with a CVSS v4.0 score of 9.2. Affecting all releases prior to versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35, the bugs stem from improper control flow during out-of-memory and fatal error handling via longjmp(). Active exploitation in the wild has been reported by watchTowr and Cloudflare, though weaponization depends heavily on server architecture and memory randomization. Finding and patching every PHP instance across operating systems, containers, and bundled stacks remains the primary operational challenge.
items.bottom_line: Unauthenticated attackers can achieve remote code execution on any server running unpatched PHP via crafted web requests.

items.title: Gheist Uses Stolen GitHub Tokens to Steal Private Repository Secrets via Actions Logs
items.one_liner: Attackers are using stolen GitHub tokens to automate the theft of secrets from private repositories by abusing Actions logs.
items.summary: An automated campaign dubbed 'Gheist' is exploiting stolen GitHub tokens to compromise private repositories and enterprise environments. Attackers plant malicious workflows that print repository secrets into GitHub Actions logs, which are then downloaded and deleted to hide the activity. The campaign has compromised over 850 accounts and planted more than 13,500 branches, often using the stolen secrets to enumerate cloud credentials. Because the exfiltration occurs entirely within GitHub's infrastructure, it bypasses traditional network-based security controls.
items.bottom_line: If your GitHub token is compromised, attackers can silently extract all repository secrets via Actions logs without triggering external network alerts.

items.one_liner: Mistral releases Mistral Large 4, a 1T-parameter open-weight model with strong cybersecurity and vulnerability-patching capabilities.
items.summary: Mistral Large 4, codenamed Le Chonk, is a multimodal, multilingual Mixture-of-Experts open-weight model featuring approximately 1-trillion total parameters, 49 billion active parameters, and a 1-million token context window. Distributed under the Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License, the model excels in cybersecurity tasks, scoring 82 percent on the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index by successfully reproducing and patching vulnerabilities. Its architecture combines Multi-head Latent Attention with a DeepSeek Sparse Attention indexer, providing defensive security practitioners with a powerful local tool for vulnerability research and malware analysis.
items.bottom_line: Mistral Large 4 provides defenders with a powerful open-weight LLM capable of reproducing vulnerabilities and analyzing malware locally.

items.title: Hackers Infect 953 Online Stores With Scanner-Evading JavaScript, Mostly on Magento
items.one_liner: A persistent e-commerce malware campaign has compromised nearly a thousand Magento stores using bot-filtering JavaScript loaders.
items.summary: An ongoing campaign active since July 2025 has infected 953 online stores, predominantly running Magento, with scanner-evading malicious JavaScript loaders. Dutch security firm Sansec discovered that attackers inject malicious stubs into Magento's `cms_block` database table, utilizing five distinct domains including `deepveindrilling[.]com` to serve payloads. The injected scripts perform browser fingerprinting and environment checks to filter out security scanners and bots, ensuring payloads are delivered exclusively to real shoppers. Initial access to at least 471 stores was achieved by exploiting vulnerabilities such as PolyShell (CVE-2026-48356) and SessionReaper (CVE-2025-54236).
items.bottom_line: Attackers are actively exploiting unpatched Magento vulnerabilities like PolyShell to inject persistent, scanner-evading JavaScript loaders into online stores.

items.title: CVE-2026-114349: Apache Kafka: Denial of service via unbounded memory allocation when decoding compressed record batches
items.one_liner: Apache Kafka is vulnerable to a DoS attack where a small malicious payload forces massive memory allocation, requiring both a patch and manual configuration to mitigate.
items.summary: A critical denial-of-service vulnerability (CVE-2026-114349) in Apache Kafka allows attackers to trigger an OutOfMemoryError by sending a small, crafted compressed record batch that declares a massive decompressed size. This forces the broker to allocate up to 2 GiB of memory per request, which can crash request-handler threads or the log-cleaner thread, effectively halting log compaction. The vulnerability affects versions 0.11.0.0 through 4.3.1. Mitigation requires upgrading to patched versions and explicitly configuring the `max.decompressed.message.bytes` limit, as it defaults to an unlimited state.
items.bottom_line: Upgrading Kafka is insufficient; you must also set a bounded value for `max.decompressed.message.bytes` to prevent memory exhaustion attacks.

claims.text: The size is attacker-controlled, and the batch CRC does not constrain it, so a small (around 90-byte), CRC-valid compressed produce request can declare a body size of up to about 2 GiB and force the broker to attempt that allocation, raising OutOfMemoryError.
claims.support_span: The size is attacker-controlled, and the batch CRC does not constrain it, so a small (around 90-byte), CRC-valid compressed produce request can declare a body size of up to about 2 GiB and force the broker to attempt that allocation, raising OutOfMemoryError.

items.title: [0day-rubbish] NUUO Crystal Server 3.19.0.85 unauthenticated upload.php PHP web-root write with fastcgi execution into server-side code execution as the web service account (9.8 Critical)
items.one_liner: An unauthenticated file write and fastcgi execution vulnerability in NUUO Crystal Server allows remote attackers to achieve root-level code execution.
items.summary: Researchers have publicly disclosed a critical 9.8-rated unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in NUUO Crystal Server version 3.19.0.85, an Ubuntu-based video management and NVR appliance. The flaw stems from an unauthenticated upload script (upload.php) that accepts arbitrary client-supplied filenames and passes them directly to the copy() function without session validation, extension checks, or path restrictions. An anonymous remote attacker can post a multipart PHP payload directly into the served web root (/NU20/web/) and subsequently trigger execution through the server's FastCGI mapping. This enables unauthenticated command execution as the web service account without requiring credentials or memory corruption primitives.
key_facts: Vulnerability Type: Unauthenticated file upload and execution (CWE-306, CWE-434, CWE-73)
items.bottom_line: NUUO Crystal Server 3.19.0.85 suffers from a critical unauthenticated file upload flaw leading to remote code execution via FastCGI mapping.

items.title: Siemens Mendix SAML Module
items.one_liner: A critical authentication bypass in Mendix SAML modules could allow unauthorized access to industrial control systems, requiring immediate patching.
items.summary: The Siemens Mendix SAML module contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to gain unauthorized access by replaying valid SAML assertions. The flaw exists in IdP-initiated authentication flows across multiple versions of the Mendix SAML module. Siemens has released updated versions to address this issue and recommends that users apply these patches immediately. Organizations should also ensure their industrial control systems are isolated from the internet and protected by firewalls.
items.bottom_line: If you manage Mendix-based industrial applications, you must update the SAML module to version 4.2.4 (for Mendix 10/11) or 3.6.29 (for Mendix 9) to prevent remote authentication bypass.

items.title: ZDI-26-834: Linux Kernel IPv6 AH Routing Header Integer Underflow Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability
items.one_liner: A local privilege escalation in the Linux kernel IPv6 AH routing header parser lets low-privileged code execute arbitrary commands as the kernel.
items.summary: An integer underflow vulnerability in the Linux kernel's IPv6 AH routing header parser allows low-privileged local attackers to execute arbitrary code with kernel privileges. The flaw stems from insufficient validation of user-supplied data before buffer allocation, which can be triggered via ipv6_rt_hdr headers. Linux has released a patch to address the issue. Affected systems could face complete compromise if an attacker establishes low-privileged code execution.
items.bottom_line: Linux kernel installations must be updated immediately to prevent local users from achieving full kernel-level code execution via IPv6 AH routing header parsing flaws.

items.one_liner: An unauthenticated stack-based buffer overflow in Alpine iLX-F511 allows root RCE via Android Auto.
items.summary: A critical stack-based buffer overflow zero-day vulnerability (ZDI-26-827) exists in the Android Auto connection handler of Alpine iLX-F511 devices. The flaw stems from a lack of proper length validation on user-supplied data prior to copying it into a fixed-length stack-based buffer. Physically present attackers can exploit this vulnerability without authentication to execute arbitrary code with root privileges. After the vendor requested an extension and failed to provide a fix following disclosure, the Zero Day Initiative published the advisory as a 0-day, recommending that interaction with the device be restricted.
items.bottom_line: Restrict physical access and interaction with Alpine iLX-F511 units immediately, as this zero-day root RCE is publicly disclosed without a patch.

items.title: Japan Airlines suffers third-party data breach exposing passenger info
items.one_liner: A long-term vulnerability in the Amadeus booking system has led to a significant data breach across multiple major international airlines.
items.summary: Japan Airlines (JAL) confirmed a data breach involving its third-party provider, Amadeus, which exposed the personal information of approximately 92,000 passengers. The breach occurred between August 2023 and September 2026 due to a vulnerability in Amadeus's travel booking display environment. While most victims had only reservation codes and flight details exposed, 2,000 customers had sensitive data stolen, including passport numbers and contact information. Other major airlines, including ANA, Asiana, and Korean Air, have also been impacted by the same vulnerability.

items.one_liner: CISA has added a VMware logging bypass and a Linux kernel privilege escalation flaw to its KEV catalog, with mandatory patching deadlines.
items.summary: CISA has added two critical vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog: CVE-2026-41709 in Broadcom VMware ESXi and CVE-2026-46300 in the Linux Kernel. The VMware flaw, exploited by the China-linked threat actor Warp Panda, allows attackers with administrative privileges to bypass audit logging to hide malicious activity. The Linux Kernel vulnerability, known as 'Fragnesia', allows local unprivileged attackers to corrupt the kernel page cache and gain full root access. Federal agencies are mandated to remediate these flaws by November 11 and October 31, 2026, respectively.

items.title: Inside "MR ROBOT" - Anatomy of a Malware-as-a-Service Operation Targeting Indian Bank Customers
items.one_liner: MR ROBOT is a rented Android Malware-as-a-Service platform targeting Indian banking customers with SMS interception and *21# call forwarding.
items.summary: MR ROBOT is an active, multi-tenant Android Malware-as-a-Service (MaaS) operation targeting Indian bank customers via rented crimeware platforms, Telegram bots, and web control panels. Affiliates use personalized APK builders to distribute fake banking, utility, and government applications that sideload an encrypted second-stage trojan. The malware intercepts SMS and OTPs, activates unconditional *21# call forwarding to bypass phone-based 2FA, and deploys phishing overlays to harvest credentials. Investigators tracked active deployment campaigns with hundreds of compromised devices and thousands of intercepted messages per tenant.

items.bottom_line: Indian financial institutions and users face active targeting from the MR ROBOT MaaS operation, which systematically defeats SMS- and call-based 2FA.

The flaw allows a malicious authenticated administrator to store or execute JavaScript payloads through the web interface. Risk is minimized when management interfaces are restricted to trusted internal IP addresses or jump boxes. items.one_liner: Go applications on Linux default to enabling MPTCP, which can expose them to kernel RCE vulnerabilities like CVE-2026-98432.
items.summary: A use-after-free vulnerability affecting IPv4 TCP connection handling in the Linux kernel, designated CVE-2026-98432, can be leveraged for remote code execution when Multipath TCP listeners are exposed. The Go security team noted that starting with Go 1.24, Go programs enable MPTCP by default for listen sockets on Linux, heightening potential exposure. items.title: The Doorway Botnet: Inside a Large-Scale IoT and Network Device Compromise Campaign
items.one_liner: CloudSEK exposed the 'Doorway' IoT botnet operation, a Rust-based modular scanning and exploitation framework recruiting devices for proxies.
items.summary: A CloudSEK investigation uncovered an active IoT exploitation and proxy-building operation known as 'Doorway' through exposed open directory workspaces containing 41 GB of operational data. The infrastructure hosts a modular Rust-based scanning engine comprising nearly 21,870 lines of code and 59 exploit modules targeting cameras, routers, ONUs, and Java services. Operational ledgers revealed extensive compromise metrics, including 4,671 module-level join records across 4,217 IP addresses and 7,369 successful MikroTik/RouterOS authentications. The structured campaign relies on automated reconnaissance and credential stuffing to build and maintain a proxy network.

items.bottom_line: Network administrators must secure exposed IoT devices and routers against automated credential stuffing and exploit modules used by the Doorway botnet.

items.title: Amd uProof EoP kernel driver vuln https://github.com/mein-0/MercilessAmd @secharvester
items.one_liner: A signed AMD uProf driver lets local users overwrite MSRs and achieve ring-0 execution via an unvalidated IOCTL interface.
items.summary: A signed kernel driver, AmdTools64.sys, shipping with AMD uProf allows standard users with an open handle to read and write arbitrary Model Specific Registers without index validation. An attacker can leverage the 0xFFF02804 and 0xFFF02808 IOCTLs to overwrite the IA32_LSTAR syscall address, bypass SMEP using existing code gadgets, and execute arbitrary shellcode at CPL0 to copy the SYSTEM token into the current process. The exploit was tested successfully on Windows 10 x64 22H2 (build 19045.6456) using AMD uProf 5.3.521.0 and driver version 1.7.16.218, though Windows 11 VBS/HVCI blocks the wrmsr instruction when Memory Integrity is enabled. The researcher disclosed the issue to AMD PSIRT, who blocked their Gmail address in response.
items.bottom_line: A signed AMD profiling driver contains an arbitrary MSR read/write vulnerability that allows local privilege escalation to NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM on Windows 10.

claims.text: AmdTools64.sys allows reading and writing arbitrary MSRs with no index validation via IOCTLs 0xFFF02804 and 0xFFF02808.
claims.support_span: There are two IOCTLs and that is the whole story. 0xFFF02804 reads an MSR and 0xFFF02808 writes one, both with a 20-byte buffer and no index validation.

claims.text: The exploit overwrites IA32_LSTAR to run shellcode at CPL0, copying the SYSTEM token into the current process.
claims.support_span: Point it at code you control and the next syscall runs your code at CPL0. SMEP is the only thing in the way, so the exploit reads IA32_LSTAR first to find ntoskrnl, parses the import directory from disk, finds a couple of gadgets to clear SMEP with mov cr4, rax, runs a small shellcode that copies the SYSTEM token into the current process, and restores IA32_LSTAR on the way out so the machine keeps working.

claims.text: The vulnerability was tested on Windows 10 x64 22H2 with AMD uProf 5.3.521.0 and driver version 1.7.16.218.
claims.support_span: I tested this on Windows 10 x64 22H2 (build 19045.6456) with AMD uProf 5.3.521.0. The driver is version 1.7.16.218.

The vulnerability, which allows unauthenticated remote code execution, was exploited as a zero-day by the ShinyHunters group (tracked as UNC6240) against universities and other sectors before a June 2026 patch. The attack chain uses a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) to bypass trust checks on an internal management interface, enabling the deployment of web shells or malicious XML files. Oracle is currently working to assign separate CVE identifiers to the individual components of the chain.
items.bottom_line: The complexity of the PeopleSoft exploit chain demonstrates how SSRF can be leveraged to bypass internal security boundaries and achieve full system compromise.

items.title: Can we trust LLMs to judge whether a research idea is novel?
items.one_liner: Evaluating LLM novelty judges reveals that their verdicts on scientific research ideas are highly unstable and vulnerable to minor prompt alterations.
items.summary: Researchers released a new study titled Old Ideas, Novel Problems examining how reliably large language models evaluate the scientific novelty of research ideas. To construct a reliable benchmark, the team mined ICLR 2026 peer reviews for explicit reviewer discussions of originality, establishing a high-novelty pool of 154 accepted papers and a lower-novelty pool of 145 papers. Evaluating six LLM judges—including GPT versions and Claude Sonnet/Opus models—revealed that minor prompt wording changes can shift accuracy by over 50 percentage points. Furthermore, additional reasoning budgets and retrieval systems failed to consistently improve novelty evaluation performance.
items.bottom_line: LLMs cannot yet serve as dependable novelty judges for automated scientific discovery without more robust evaluation methods.

claims.text: Today we’re releasing Old Ideas, Novel Problems, a new study of how reliably large language models can evaluate the novelty of scientific research ideas.

items.title: How I Found a $113,337 AF_ALG Linux Local Privilege Escalation Before Copy Fail
items.one_liner: A retrospective look at uncovering a $113,337 Linux kernel privilege escalation flaw in the AF_ALG cryptographic subsystem via unprivileged socket APIs.
items.summary: Security researcher Muhammad Alifa Ramdhan details the discovery of CVE-2025-39964, a critical race condition vulnerability in the Linux kernel's AF_ALG cryptographic subsystem that earned a $113,337 reward via Google's kernelCTF. Exploiting out-of-bounds access stemming from how AF_ALG handles inputs across unprivileged sockets, an ordinary user can escalate privileges to root or achieve container escape. Present in the kernel since 2011, this vulnerability preceded the widely known 'Copy Fail' flaw but highlights the same underlying kernel attack surface.
items.bottom_line: Unprivileged access to the Linux kernel's AF_ALG subsystem harbors deep race condition vulnerabilities capable of full privilege escalation and container escape.

items.title: Which LLM writes the best code? A 2026 comparison
items.one_liner: Adopt an empirical pilot framework instead of static leaderboards to evaluate coding LLMs for your specific repository context.
items.summary: Finding the best coding LLM requires an empirical decision framework rather than relying on stale public leaderboards, given the rapid release cycles from providers like Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, and SpaceXAI. Teams should define their specific tasks, pin exact model versions, and run pilots directly on internal repositories to measure acceptance rates rather than subjective impressions. Evaluation criteria should include code correctness, security vulnerabilities, maintainability, repository context awareness, latency, cost, and governance. With approximately 80% of developers utilizing multiple AI tools and frequently switching, managing multiple models concurrently has become an operational norm.

items.bottom_line: Public AI coding leaderboards are obsolete; teams must run structured repository pilots assessing correctness, security, and cost.

items.one_liner: Former GitHub CEO launches Entire, a Git forge built for AI agent workflows, backed by a $60M seed round.
items.summary: GitHub experienced 257 infrastructure incidents between May 2025 and April 2026, driven by high traffic volumes from AI coding agents generating 17 million monthly pull requests. items.one_liner: Compact open-source LLMs specialized in aging biology matched or surpassed larger frontier AI models on a new multi-omics benchmark.

items.title: OpenBSD 8.0 Released With Major Security Hardening and Post-Quantum SSH Support
items.one_liner: OpenBSD 8.0 introduces post-quantum signature support in OpenSSH, core memory randomization, and extensive hardening patches across its stack.
items.summary: OpenBSD 8.0 has been released with comprehensive security fixes across its kernel, PF firewall, and network services, alongside experimental post-quantum SSH support. The 61st release features OpenSSH 10.6 with experimental composite mldsa44-ed25519 signature schemes and disabled LZ77 dictionary coding to prevent side-channel leaks. LibreSSL 4.4.0 is included, establishing X25519MLKEM768 as the preferred TLS 1.3 group and patching certificate issues. Additionally, the release implements direct memory map randomization on amd64 architectures, fixes kernel stack info leaks, and hardens firmware verification and archive extraction defenses.
items.bottom_line: Administrators must review breaking compatibility changes and errata before upgrading systems to OpenBSD 8.0 due to significant kernel hardening and crypto protocol adjustments.

items.one_liner: Tsinghua's open-source AKV caching server reduces LLM agent costs by 27.7% via granular KV cache manipulation on SGLang.
items.summary: Researchers from Tsinghua University and CUHK have open-sourced AKV, an SGLang-based serving system designed for KV cache engineering in LLM agents. Instead of summarizing old conversation history, AKV allows agents to drop selected KV cache entries and reuse the remainder through append, drop, and reposition operations. items.bottom_line: Developers running LLM agents can lower inference costs and preserve critical context details without resorting to aggressive history summarization.

items.summary: Alexander A. Shvedov disclosed a heap use-after-free vulnerability, designated CVE-2025-60482, in GPAC's MP4Box tool during AC-4 descriptor cleanup. items.summary: El Salvador has deployed more than 2,000 soldiers to Haiti as part of a mission to retrieve four Salvadoran air force technicians who went missing after being ambushed by armed gangs in the Croix-des-Bouquets area while working with the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force. President Nayib Bukele communicated the robust deployment to Haitian Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aime, stating the troops will also assist local security efforts against gangs. Tensions rose after Haiti handed over four bodies that Bukele rejected as mismatched. The deployment comes amid severe gang violence that killed over 5,700 people in Haiti this year.

items.title: Deploying a Local Ghidra Server for Your Malware Analysis Lab, (Thu, Oct 29th)
items.one_liner: Setting up a local Ghidra Server in your lab preserves malware analysis progress across VM snapshots and enables multi-analyst collaboration.
items.summary: Deploying a local Ghidra Server in a malware analysis lab prevents data loss when analysis VMs are reverted to clean snapshots. Ghidra Server turns local `.gpr` projects into shared repositories backed by central storage, enabling versioning, multi-client access, team collaboration, and local confidentiality. The lightweight Java-based service can run in a separate Linux container or VM using JDK 21 or newer, listening on ports TCP/13100 and TCP/13101.
key_facts: Requirements: JDK 21 or newer, Linux VM/container
items.bottom_line: Malware analysts should deploy a dedicated Ghidra Server to ensure analysis annotations persist safely outside ephemeral lab virtual machines.

items.title: Europe's youth is on the march - but does anything actually unite them?
items.one_liner: Youth-led protests driven by cost-of-living and education grievances are spreading across European cities, coordinated via social media.
items.summary: A wave of student and youth-led protests has erupted across European cities including Milan, Marseille, Madrid, Rome, Florence, Lisbon, and Brussels, driven by grievances over education standards, social inequality, and the rising cost of living. Many of these demonstrations have turned violent, resulting in clashes, looting, police intervention with tear gas and water cannons, and a high proportion of minor arrests. Officials and observers have noted the ad hoc organization of these movements via platforms like TikTok and Instagram—coined the "TikTokisation" of protests—with participants drawing inspiration from cross-border peer movements.
items.bottom_line: Widespread, youth-led protests over economic and educational grievances are causing social and political volatility across multiple European countries.

items.title: Building boom puts 300,000 people in the path of potential Himalayan disasters
items.one_liner: Unchecked construction in Himalayan high-risk zones puts over 300,000 people in the path of floods and disasters.
items.summary: A peer-reviewed study in Scientific Reports indicates that at least 300,000 people in the Himalayan region are living in potential disaster zones due to a rapid building boom. Researchers found that built-up land in high-risk zones across northern Nepal, parts of southeastern Tibet, and India's Uttarakhand grew by 45% between 2016 and 2023. In areas threatened by glacial lake flooding, development surged by nearly 78% over the same timeframe. Unregulated tourism infrastructure and hydropower plant construction are significantly compounding disaster risks.
key_facts: Glacial lake flood zone development increase: ~78%
items.bottom_line: Rapid, unplanned infrastructure expansion near Himalayan river valleys dramatically escalates vulnerability to glacial floods and landslides.

items.summary: AI agent identity and management startup Mintive has secured an $11 million total raise, highlighted by a $7 million seed round led by Cowboy Ventures with participation from Coatue, Operator Collective, Hustle Fund, Jeff Dean, Andrej Karpathy, and Frederic Kerrest. Founded by former Google Brain engineers Jiquan Ngiam and Vijay Vasudevan, Mintive provides an enterprise platform featuring an MCP gateway for service access authorization, an LLM gateway for cost control and routing, an agent identity manager, and a monitoring dashboard. The startup has onboarded 50 enterprise customers since its February launch, distinguishing itself through simplified setup and access control.
key_facts: Seed Round: $7 million led by Cowboy Ventures
items.bottom_line: Mintive has raised $11 million to offer enterprise AI governance, model routing, and permissioning infrastructure for autonomous agents.

items.title: US Fed Chair Kevin Warsh to bring major change to FOMC’s 2027 meeting schedule? What does it mean for rate decisions?
items.one_liner: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh restructures the 2027 FOMC meeting schedule to include dedicated long-term monetary strategy sessions.
items.summary: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh announced a revision to the U.S. central bank's 2027 meeting schedule, maintaining eight total meetings annually but dedicating one exclusively to monetary policy strategy discussions without interest rate votes or policy statements. The structural change aims to give policymakers extended horizons to examine major economic questions and balance near-term data assessments with longer-term goals. Warsh reiterated the Fed's commitment to achieving its 2% inflation target while noting that price stability cannot be judged by isolated calendar dates or single data points.
items.bottom_line: Modifying the FOMC meeting agenda to separate strategy discussions from rate decisions institutionalizes a broader horizon for U.S. monetary policy.

items.title: Nifty premium slips as traders brace for renewed West Asia tensions
items.one_liner: Nifty rollover costs hit a five-month low as traders brace for potential West Asia energy shocks.
items.summary: Indian traders reduced risk exposure as the Nifty’s rollover cost for the October series sank to a five-month low of 0.29%, down from 0.78% in September. The decline highlights reduced optimism and caution among traders entering the November series, driven by elevated crude oil prices and fears of renewed US-Iran hostilities following the November 3 US midterms. Crude prices remain a key macroeconomic headwind, impacting India's current account deficit and currency stability. While the benchmark Nifty 50 is down 12.2% year-to-date, it recently rose 1% to 22,936.75, with derivative data indicating a neutral-to-cautious market setup.
items.bottom_line: Nifty rollover costs dropped to a five-month low as traders hedge against potential crude price spikes and West Asian military escalations.

items.title: Energy Giant Engie Notifies Customers of Supply Chain Breach
items.one_liner: A supply chain data breach at a partner marketing platform exposed personal data for Engie customers, creating phishing risks.
items.summary: French natural gas multinational Engie suffered a third-party supply chain data breach exposing customer personal details such as names, postal and email addresses, telephone numbers, and unique energy supply IDs. The company stated that its own internal IT systems were not compromised, attributing the incident instead to a marketing platform used by partners that was accessed by unauthorized actors. No banking information was involved, and no extortion group has claimed responsibility for the incident yet. Engie has disabled the affected access, launched an investigation, and warned affected customers to watch out for potential fraud and phishing.
items.bottom_line: Engie customers must be alert to targeted phishing and impersonation attempts following a third-party marketing platform data exposure.

items.title: AI Security Scoping: Define What To Test In Your Deployment
items.one_liner: AI security scoping must be tied to specific business risk decisions to avoid superficial testing and unaddressed operational vulnerabilities.
items.summary: Effective AI security requires moving beyond generic 'AI checks' toward structured scoping that aligns testing methods with specific business risk decisions. Organizations should categorize testing into AI penetration testing, architecture reviews, and red teaming based on the deployment's maturity and exposure. The full stack—including models, RAG pipelines, agents, and identity controls—must be evaluated to ensure defensible security outcomes. As AI features move from pilot to production, the attack surface expands, necessitating a comprehensive ecosystem view rather than focusing solely on the model boundary.
items.bottom_line: Treating AI security as a single 'check' is a failure; security must be scoped to the entire stack, including data pipelines, agents, and infrastructure, to be effective.

claims.text: AI security scoping starts with the risk decision (ship, gate, expand, or mitigate) and picks the method that can answer it with evidence.

items.title: TightVNC Viewer Pre-auth RCE https://ssd-disclosure.com/tightvnc-viewer-pre-auth-rce/ @secharvester
items.summary: Summary In VNC the server announces the screen size and the viewer allocates a pixel buffer for it. TightVNC computes that buffer’s byte size in a 32-bit int. A server announcing 32768 x 32769 at 32bpp makes the size wrap from 4 GB to 128 KB, while the viewer keeps the announced dimensions as its logical canvas. Pixel writes are then placed by 32-bit pointer arithmetic against the announced width, into the 128 KB allocation, with no bounds check. That is a server-controlled write at any signed offset from the framebuffer.
